runtime_audit.interpretation: Runtime records describe only the observed or blocked UI states under their stated model, firmware, platform and fixture conditions. Static availability, historical screenshots and source audit fields remain preserved; absence of a runtime record is not verification.

availability_semantics.yes: User-facing implementation is exposed in the audited source; ordinary prerequisites still apply.
availability_semantics.conditional: Exposed only with listed device, OS, account, network, provider, rollout or experiment conditions.
availability_semantics.no: Explicitly unsupported or absent from the audited user-facing composition; not a claim about future releases.
availability_semantics.unknown: Source evidence is insufficient for a defensible parity claim.

metadata.scope: Suite desktop, Suite web and native mobile; SDK examples and backend internals excluded. Mobile means native app, not a phone browser.
metadata.ownership_semantics: Product teams inferred from QA streams/domain; CODEOWNERS on roots means code-review ownership, not accountable product ownership.
metadata.link_policy: Local links identify this exact checkout. GitHub links use the published ancestor only for unchanged files; newer local files have no GitHub URL.

desktop_automated.rationale: On desktop/web, application onboarding is the initial analytics choice (onboarding.analytics). Active tests check that the consent screen appears on any initially visited route (/accounts, web). They also check that it stays after reload until confirmed and that completion persists after reload. Both choices are honored: disabling in onboarding sends only the analytics-disable event and the switch stays off after reload; keeping it enabled sends suite-ready/analytics events. Only limited gaps remain.
covered_intents: First-launch consent remains after reload until confirmed; initialized-device onboarding and completion persist after reload.
Disable analytics in onboarding: only the analytics disable event is sent and the setting remains off after reload.
Keep analytics enabled in onboarding: suite-ready and analytics events are sent.
Consent appears on any initially visited route and continuing leads to a usable wallet.
gaps: First-run failure/error states and the any-route consent check on Electron (that test is @webOnly) are not covered.

evidence.scenario: Until user passed through initial run, it will be there after reload
evidence.verification: Consent toggle visible, still visible after reload, continue leads to complete-onboarding; after reload the consent is hidden and the complete-onboarding button stays visible.

evidence.scenario: should respect disabled analytics in onboarding with following enabling in settings
evidence.verification: Switch analytics off in onboarding; the analytics request has value false; after reload the settings switch is unchecked.

evidence.scenario: should respect enabled analytics in onboarding with following disabling in settings
evidence.verification: Continue with analytics enabled; suite-ready and analytics events are captured and the settings switch is checked.

evidence.scenario: analytics consent appears on any route that is visited initially. this time /accounts
evidence.verification: The consent heading is visible on /accounts; continuing and passing device checks reaches the dashboard and an account send form.

features.name: Passphrase Caps Lock warning
features.description: See a 'Caps Lock is on' note under the passphrase field while typing a passphrase in Suite with Caps Lock active.
features.platform_notes: Desktop and web share PassphraseInputCard, which is used by the add-hidden-wallet passphrase entry (EnterPassphrase), the empty-wallet confirmation (PassphraseWalletConfirmation) and the global Confirm passphrase modal (ConfirmPassphraseBeforeAction). The state comes from KeyboardEvent/MouseEvent.getModifierState('CapsLock'). It is read only on a window keydown while the field is focused or on a mousedown on the input, and it is cleared on blur. So autofocusing the field alone does not show the note; the user must press a key or click the field. The note is hidden while a too-long or non-ASCII error is shown. The native mobile app has no equivalent app-level warning. suite-native/forms SecureTextInputField only makes room for the iOS system Caps Lock indicator, and Android is the scored mobile platform.

desktop_manual.rationale: The desktop Security settings section contains MEV protection and Dust phishing protection (SettingsGeneral.tsx). The MEV procedure covers enable and disable with routing checks plus a BTC send with protection disabled. The transaction-list procedure checks that dust below the limit is blurred and that a manual dust limit updates the list. Both controls have a happy path with some variants, but material gaps remain.
covered_intents: Enable MEV protection, send ETH and verify protected routing in blinklabs; disable and verify the unprotected route; with MEV disabled, send from a BTC account and confirm successful broadcast.
Verify below-threshold transactions are blurred; set a manual dust limit and verify the transaction list updates.
gaps: Non-ETH sends with MEV protection enabled, protected-route failure/fallback, dust protection enable/disable, threshold boundaries and persistence of security settings are not prescribed.

evidence.scenario: Enable MEV protection, send ETH and verify protected routing in blinklabs; disable and verify the unprotected route; with MEV disabled, send from a BTC account and confirm successful broadcast.
evidence.verification: Enable MEV protection, send ETH and verify protected routing in blinklabs; disable and verify the unprotected route; with MEV disabled, send from a BTC account and confirm successful broadcast.

evidence.scenario: Verify below-threshold transactions are blurred; set a manual dust limit and verify the transaction list updates.
evidence.verification: Verify below-threshold transactions are blurred; set a manual dust limit and verify the transaction list updates.

android_manual.rationale: The native Security screen (SettingsSecurityScreen.tsx) contains the MEV protection toggle and the dust phishing threshold card; network reserve is under Settings > Advanced, so it is not evidence here. The MEV procedure covers enable, protected send, disable, unprotected send and a BTC send. The dust procedure covers enable, the suspicious-transaction display, a threshold change and disable. Material gaps remain.
covered_intents: Enable MEV protection, send ETH through the protected route, disable and repeat without protection; with protection disabled, send from a BTC account and verify successful broadcast.
Enable dust filtering, inspect suspicious low-value transactions, change threshold to a different set and disable to restore normal display.
gaps: MEV routing proof is loosely specified; protected-route failures, unsupported networks, dust threshold boundaries and persistence after restart are not prescribed.

features.name: Electrum over Tor
features.description: Connect Bitcoin, Bitcoin Testnet or Regtest to a custom Electrum server at a .onion address, routing the connection through Tor.
features.platform_notes: Desktop: the Electrum backend type is offered only when isDesktop() is true. If Tor is off and every entered URL is an onion address, Confirm opens TorModal, which offers 'Enable Tor and confirm' or 'Use default backends'. Turning Tor off later strips the onion URLs from onion-only custom backends after the disable-tor modal. Web: the Electrum type is filtered out and bundled Tor is unavailable. Mobile: Electrum is listed when the network's backendOptions include it. The app has no bundled Tor. It only detects '.onion:' in the address and, on a Backend_Error, shows 'make sure Orbot is running', so routing depends on an external Tor/VPN app such as Orbot. Electrum is configured for btc, test and regtest. Onion detection is not specific to Electrum: it applies to any custom backend URL.

navigation.desktop: Settings > Networks > Bitcoin settings (gear) > Backends type 'Custom Electrum server' > enter <host>.onion:<port>:t > Confirm > (Tor off) Enable Tor and confirm
navigation.mobile: Settings > Networks > Bitcoin sliders icon > Server type 'Electrum' > Server address <host>.onion:<port>:t > Connect (with Orbot routing the device traffic)

evidence.detail: The electrum backend option is kept only when isDesktop(), so web never offers Electrum.
Bitcoin backendOptions include electrum. Testnet (line 83) and Regtest (line 122) include it too.
hasOnlyOnions() is true when every URL, including the pending input, has a .onion hostname (isOnionUrl/parseHostname handles the host:port:t Electrum format).
On Confirm with Tor off and only onion URLs, the TorModal opens instead of saving. 'enable-tor' dispatches toggleTorThunk(true) and then saves (line 80). 'use-defaults' resets the type to default.
The 'Enable Tor and confirm' button is rendered only on desktop. The modal explains 'This backend uses an onion address...' (line 46) and offers 'Use default backends'.

features.name: Asset detail Earn offer
features.description: On an eligible asset's detail, see a staking or yield-vault offer with the current APY, open Earn from it, or dismiss it; a dismissed token yield offer stays hidden for that token.
features.platform_notes: Two banners sit below the balance/Earn section of the asset detail on both platforms. (1) Staking banner, for a stakeable native coin (no contract) with at least one account that is not staking. Desktop/web: AssetDetailStakingBanner > AssetDetailAccountsStakingBanner > useStakingBanner picks a variant. On ETH with an enabled wrapped-native yield vault it shows the 'earnEth' variant (EarnEthBannerView: 'Earn up to {apy}% APY on your ETH' with the higher of the staking rate and best vault APY, 'Explore' button). Otherwise it shows StakingBannerView with the staking APY (APR for Tron), potential yearly rewards and 'Explore staking'. Rendering waits until the vault query settles. Mobile: AssetDetailStakingBanner shows EthEarnPromoBanner (max of vault and staking APY) when the ETH account has a native yield vault, or else AssetDetailStakingRewardsBanner with the staking rate (APR wording for Tron) and potential rewards, which are redacted in discreet mode. (2) Token yield banner, for a token whose best enabled yield vault has an available APY. AssetDetailYieldBanner shows the APY with the token symbol, 'Deposit your {symbol} in a yield vault and earn rewards on it.' and 'Explore'. Explore opens Earn: on desktop/web the suite-earn route, on mobile a navigation reset to the Earn tab. Close dismisses the banner. A token yield banner is dismissed per network+contract key: desktop flags.closedTokenYieldBanners is saved by storageMiddleware; mobile bannerFlags.closedTokenYieldBannerKeys is persisted. The staking banner is dismissed per network. Desktop uses the stakeEth/Sol/Cardano/TronBannerClosed or earnEthBannerClosed flags, which it shares with the account-view staking banner. Mobile uses closedEarnBannerSymbols through EarnPromoBanner's default close. Explore and close report yield/navigate (from 'asset-detail-banner') or staking navigate analytics events. Mobile staking Explore reports navigateFlowEvent.

navigation.mobile: Home > Select a stakeable coin or a token with a yield vault > Earn banner > Explore (or Close)

evidence.detail: The desktop/web asset detail page renders AssetDetailStakingBanner and, on line 55, AssetDetailYieldBanner for the routed asset key.
canStake requires a native coin (no contract) on a supported staking network; the banner renders only for its non-staking (unstaked) accounts.

The earnEth variant renders EarnEthBannerView and reports yieldNavigateEvent from asset-detail-banner. Otherwise StakingBannerView renders (line 65) and reports stakingNavigateEvent. Both Explore buttons go to the suite-earn route.

getKind waits for the vault query. It prefers earnEth when a wrapped-native vault exists (unless earnEthBannerClosed). Otherwise it hides the banner if the per-network closed flag is set, every account is staking or there are no staking limits. close (line 82) sets the matching flag.

The token yield banner hides for coins, for a dismissed bannerKey `${networkSymbol}-${contract}` and when no vault APY is available. Explore goes to suite-earn. close (line 73) dispatches closeTokenYieldBanner(bannerKey).
Vault APY is fetched only for Ethereum-type networks while message-system yield deposit is not disabled; the best enabled vault for the token (or wrapped native) supplies the APY.
Desktop closeTokenYieldBanner records the dismissed token key in closedTokenYieldBanners. storageMiddleware.ts line 593 saves it with the other suite settings.
The mobile asset detail list header (AssetDetailScreen line 30) renders AssetDetailStakingBanner, then AssetDetailYieldBanner on line 17.
Mobile renders EthEarnPromoBanner when the account has a native yield vault, else AssetDetailStakingRewardsBanner; Explore uses useNavigateToEarn (reset to the Earn tab).
Mobile staking banner accounts are empty unless the asset is a staking-supported native coin with a stakeable product descriptor and the network banner has not been closed (closedEarnBannerSymbols).
Mobile staking offer shows the network staking rate (APR wording for Tron) and potential rewards, redacted in discreet mode.

The mobile token yield banner hides for coins, a dismissed token key or an unavailable vault APY. Explore reports yield/navigate continue and resets to Earn. close (line 82) dispatches setIsTokenYieldBannerClosed(bannerKey).
setIsTokenYieldBannerClosed stores the token key in closedTokenYieldBannerKeys, which is in bannerFlagsPersistWhitelist (line 117) and persisted by suite-native-app/state/src/reducers.ts line 446.
Jest unit test (not E2E): the token banner shows the vault APY and symbol and is absent for a token without a vault, for a coin and once dismissed (line 138).
Jest unit test (not Detox): pressing close dispatches setIsTokenYieldBannerClosed for that token key only and reports yield/navigate cancel; Explore navigation is tested on line 124.

Jest unit test (not Detox): mobile staking banner rewards, discreet redaction, Tron APR, ETH vault variant (line 269), Explore (line 284), hidden when every account stakes, after network dismissal (line 318) or for a non-stakeable asset.
Jest unit test: a closed token yield banner is remembered for that token only.

features.name: New or lookalike recipient warning
features.description: Warn under the send-form recipient field when the entered address was never paid from this account or looks like an address-poisoning lookalike of a known counterparty.
features.platform_notes: Desktop and web share the same send-form Address component. The account's recipient history exists only for Ethereum-family (EVM) and Tron accounts that have loaded transactions; Bitcoin, Cardano, Ripple, Solana and Stellar accounts never show the warning. The warning is hidden while the address has a validation error or matches an own account (own-account label shown). Lookalike (possible poisoning) takes priority over new-recipient; a previously paid address shows the separate positive 'Last sent' hint instead. The mobile send flow has no recipient-history warning.

navigation.desktop: Dashboard > sidebar: open an Ethereum-family or Tron account with transaction history > Send > type or paste a valid address you have never paid (or a lookalike of a past counterparty) into Recipient address > warning appears under the field
navigation.web: Dashboard > sidebar: open an Ethereum-family or Tron account with transaction history > Send > type or paste a valid address you have never paid (or a lookalike of a past counterparty) into Recipient address > warning appears under the field

evidence.detail: No note unless the account, its recipient history and a recipient address that validates for the account's network are all present.
Possible poisoning is checked first (a lookalike is also new), then new recipient; otherwise the last-sent time hint.
possiblePoisoning variant: critical warning icon with TR_ADDRESS_POSSIBLE_POISONING and a Learn more link to HELP_CENTER_ZERO_VALUE_ATTACKS.
newRecipient variant: warning icon with TR_ADDRESS_NEW_RECIPIENT ('You haven't sent to this address before. Double-check it before sending.').
Lookalike = never-paid address sharing the first 3 and last 4 characters (after 0x/T prefix) with another counterparty, or an address seen only in phishing-flagged transactions.
New recipient = address absent from addresses the account signed a payment to; receiving from an address does not count.
History support only for networkType ethereum and tron; the selector returns undefined when the account has no transactions (line 57).

The send-form recipient field shows the note beneath the input (line 658) only without an address error and when the address is not an own labelled account; the hook gets the ENS-resolved address when present (line 158).
Playwright: after forward ENS resolution on a mocked ETH account, asserts the recipient-history note has exact TR_ADDRESS_NEW_RECIPIENT text; the lookalike variant is not exercised.
Co-located unit tests for isPossiblePoisoning and isNewRecipient (lookalike EVM/Tron matching, paid-address trust, phishing-only, spoofed transfers); logic-level only, not executed here.

features.name: Warn about contract recipients
features.description: See a warning when the recipient of an Ethereum-family or Tron send is a smart contract, and acknowledge the risk before continuing.
features.platform_notes: Desktop/web: the evmChecks validator of the recipient field runs for networkType ethereum (all EVM networks) and tron; it calls TrezorConnect.getAccountInfo on the typed address (or the ENS-resolved address) and returns TR_EVM_ADDRESS_IS_CONTRACT as the address hint when payload.misc.contractInfo is present, with an 'I understand the risk' button and a Learn more link to the EVM send-to-contract help article. Dismissal resets when the address changes. Offline or a failed lookup shows 'cannot verify history' instead. Mobile: useAddressValidationAlerts runs useContractAddressCheck for ethereum and tron networks once a valid address (or ENS-resolved address) is entered and any token alert was shown; it shows a 'This is a smart contract address.' alert with an 'I understand' button. A failed lookup is silently ignored on mobile. Solana uses a separate associated-token-account check, not this warning.

features.name: XRP account reserve warning
features.description: See the XRP account's required unspendable reserve when the entered amount exceeds the spendable balance but not the total balance.
features.platform_notes: Desktop and web share validateReserveOrBalance -> getAmountValidationResult (suite-common): for a native XRP (and also Stellar) send, an amount above availableBalance but below the total balance shows 'Amount is above the required unspendable reserve (<reserve> XRP)'; an amount at or above the total balance shows the generic not-enough message instead. The same validator is reused by trading and staking amount inputs. Mobile computes the reserve (getRippleReserve) and has a 'ripple-higher-than-reserve' yup test, but static analysis indicates the message is masked: the test only fires when the amount exceeds availableBalance and the normal-fee max amount exists, and in that case the preceding 'is-higher-than-balance' test (fee-adjusted max <= availableBalance) also fails; yupResolver keeps the first error per field (verified ordering with yup 1.7.1 locally), so the user sees 'You don't have enough balance to send this amount.' Mobile visibility is therefore unverified (LEAD).

navigation.mobile: Home or XRP account detail > Send > enter recipient > enter an amount above the available balance (reserve-specific message likely shadowed by the generic balance error)

'ripple-higher-than-reserve' test appends the reserve to the error, but runs after 'is-higher-than-balance' (line 205), which also fails for the same amounts, so the first (generic) error is the one displayed.

evidence.detail: ClipboardCopyMenu with shareQRCodeImage, saveQRCodeImage, copy (QR image) and copyAddress actions (lines 32-54). ViewShot (line 57) wraps the QR content for PNG capture.
iOS ClipboardCopyMenu renders the menuActions in a SwiftUI ContextMenu opened by long-press on its children.

handleShareQRCode captures a PNG tmpfile and opens Share.share with the file URL. It reports the receiveQRCodeActionEvent 'share' only when the share sheet is not dismissed and shows a generic error alert on failure.
handleCopyQRCode captures a base64 PNG, puts it on the clipboard with Clipboard.setImageAsync and shows a 'QR code copied' toast.
handleSaveQRCode saves through saveQRCodeImageToPhotos and shows a 'saved to Photos' toast. On permissionDenied it shows an alert with an Open Settings button (Linking.openSettings).

Uses expo-media-library/legacy requestPermissionsAsync(true), which asks for add-only Photos permission, then saveToLibraryAsync. The app config declares NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription (suite-native-app/app/app.config.ts:308).
The Android fallback wraps the QR in ClipboardCopyMenu onCopy={onCopyAddress}, so long-press only copies the address and there are no image actions.

Renders ReceiveQRCodeCard with onCopyAddress. It is used by ReceiveAddressCard (fresh-address Receive screen, ReceiveAddressContent.tsx:119) and ReceiveAddressDetailScreen.tsx:84 (address history detail).

features.name: Inspect internal transfers
features.description: See native-coin internal transfers that a contract or program call moved to or from the account in history, and inspect their addresses and amount in transaction detail.
features.platform_notes: Not EVM-only. Internal transfers come from three sources: Blockbook ethereumSpecific.internalTransfers on EVM networks (only type-0 value transfers that touch the account, or ETH staking pool withdrawals); the EVM-RPC worker's native moves; and Solana transactions with unknown-program instructions or stake claims, computed as the account's balance change minus the fee. A Solana transfer has only the account address: 'from' is empty on received transfers and 'to' is empty on sent ones. Desktop and web show the transfers in the Inputs & outputs tab of the transaction detail modal under an 'Internal Transfers' heading. The heading renders for the ethereum, tron, solana, stellar and cardano network types when the list is non-empty. They also appear as amount rows in the Amount tab and as 'internal' targets in the history row. The modal drops instant-staking deposit transfers. Mobile shows an 'Internal transfers' group in the Inputs & outputs sheet. That sheet uses the raw list without the instant-stake filter, while the history row and the detail targets go through createTargets and are filtered.

The detail modal removes internal transfers classified as instant-staking deposits before rendering.
The Amount tab lists each internal transfer amount with its sign and fiat value.
Adds non-staking internal transfers as 'internal' targets, used by the desktop and mobile history rows and the mobile detail screen.
The desktop/web history row shows the amount of an internal target in the network coin.
filterEthereumInternalTransfers keeps only type-0 internal transfers whose from or to is the account, or ETH staking pool withdrawals.

The mobile Inputs & outputs sheet renders a separate 'Internal transfers' section; the section returns null when empty.

features.name: Inspect a simulated swap
features.description: See the Blockaid simulation status and the simulated receive amount, when one is available, before confirming a same-chain decentralized EVM swap.
features.platform_notes: Desktop/web and mobile share composeDexTxSimulationAction and useDexExchangeTxSimulation. Simulation runs only for a DEX quote from an EVM account whose network has a chainId, built either as ethereumSignTransaction from dexTx or as ethereumSignTypedData for EIP-712 sign-data quotes. It is gated by the message-system feature trading.txSimulation, which is enabled by default. The 'Simulation powered by Blockaid' subtitle and the 'Simulating transaction' loading state are hidden when simulation is off, after a simulation error and for cross-chain swaps. A cross-chain swap is still simulated on the source chain, and its result can still replace the receive amount. When the scan credits the receive asset, the simulated amount replaces the quoted receive amount. The subtitle is shown whether or not a risk issue banner appears; issues are covered by trade.swap.risk-review. On Android the status appears in the swap preview screen header, and the simulated amount appears in the 'to' account card and the slippage picker.

features.name: Manage existing swap approval
features.description: Review how much of the source token the DEX provider is already approved to spend compared with the amount the swap needs, see a warning for unlimited approvals, and either continue the swap or revoke the approval.
features.platform_notes: Desktop/web only. When the selected DEX quote needs an ERC-20 approval and an allowance for the provider's spender is already on-chain (amount > 0), the Swap form shows a 'Manage approval' text button under Continue/Swap (TradingFormApproval). It replaces the former in-form 'Revoke' button and TradingRevokeModal, which were removed in the same change. It saves the form values and opens the 'wallet-trading-exchange-allowance' route (/accounts/coinmarket/exchange/allowance). The page shows a coverage heading: '{provider} has unlimited access to your {symbol}', 'Your approval covers this swap', 'Your approval is too low for this swap', 'No approval yet' or 'Approval revoked'. A next-step description says whether to swap, approve, or reset for tokens such as USDT that cannot raise an allowance in place. A meter compares the current limit with the swap amount. Unlimited allowances show a warning banner. 'Continue swap' starts the regular approval/swap step flow. 'Revoke approval', shown only when there is an allowance, composes and signs a zero-amount revoke transaction with an editable network fee. It then shows the pending txid, which opens the transaction detail, and switches the heading to 'Approval revoked' after confirmation. If the spender is unknown, the page borrows a revoke quote from the provider and hands the quote back on leave. If the quote is missing, errored or no longer needs approval, the page redirects to the Swap form. Mobile has no equivalent page; its DEX approval and revoke steps are part of the native exchange flow.

variants.platform_notes: Desktop/web only. When the selected DEX quote needs an ERC-20 approval and an allowance for the provider's spender is already on-chain (amount > 0), the Swap form shows a 'Manage approval' text button under Continue/Swap (TradingFormApproval). It replaces the former in-form 'Revoke' button and TradingRevokeModal, which were removed in the same change. It saves the form values and opens the 'wallet-trading-exchange-allowance' route (/accounts/coinmarket/exchange/allowance). The page shows a coverage heading: '{provider} has unlimited access to your {symbol}', 'Your approval covers this swap', 'Your approval is too low for this swap', 'No approval yet' or 'Approval revoked'. A next-step description says whether to swap, approve, or reset for tokens such as USDT that cannot raise an allowance in place. A meter compares the current limit with the swap amount. Unlimited allowances show a warning banner. 'Continue swap' starts the regular approval/swap step flow. 'Revoke approval', shown only when there is an allowance, composes and signs a zero-amount revoke transaction with an editable network fee. It then shows the pending txid, which opens the transaction detail, and switches the heading to 'Approval revoked' after confirmation. If the spender is unknown, the page borrows a revoke quote from the provider and hands the quote back on leave. If the quote is missing, errored or no longer needs approval, the page redirects to the Swap form. Mobile has no equivalent page; its DEX approval and revoke steps are part of the native exchange flow.

features.platform_notes: Desktop and web share TradingDetailLayout, which mounts AfterTradeExperiment on every buy, sell and swap detail page. Mobile mounts TradingHistoryDetailAfterTradeExperiment in the order detail. On every platform ExperimentWrapper falls back to the first component (variant A, an empty fragment) when the tradingFeedbackForm experiment is missing or not assigned, so nothing appears by default. Variant B shows the rating card. The card requires both a rating and non-empty text before it submits, so the comment is not optional. Mobile opens the text entry in a bottom sheet after the user taps a rating. Variant C shows a survey card only when a valid trading.survey message-system payload exists. On mobile the survey also needs a CTA that canHandleCtaAction accepts for the current language. The card is not gated on trade completion, so it can appear on pending orders as well.

features.name: Resume an unfinished trade form
features.description: Return to an unfinished Buy, Sell or Swap form and find the amount, assets and other values you entered still filled in.
features.platform_notes: Desktop/web: selecting an offer saves the current form values to the trading Redux slice (saveFormValues). The Buy, Sell and Swap form hooks start from those saved values instead of the defaults, so the header Back button on the confirm or approval page (or the Buy confirm redirect when its quote is missing) reopens the form with the earlier values. The saved values are cleared when you switch the Buy/Sell/Swap tab, change the country of residence, re-enter Trade from outside the trading section, bind a different trading account (embedded account trade form), or reach a Buy/Sell success or failure detail or a Swap success or returned detail. Mobile: each form stays mounted under the screens pushed on top of the Trade tab, so closing a preview or review returns to the same values. The form is reset only on an explicit request: after a Buy provider response, or after a Sell/Swap signing review is cancelled or continued. Switching the Buy/Sell/Swap type unmounts the active form.

navigation.mobile: Trade tab > Buy, Sell or Swap > choose the assets and enter an amount > Continue > close or go back from the preview screen > the same form still shows the earlier values

Switching the Buy/Sell/Swap tab clears quotes and the saved values of the target type; CountrySelectModal.tsx:39 and the Buy/Sell success/failure and Swap success/returned detail views dispatch the same clear.

Switching the trade type replaces the form subtree, so the values survive only within the active form.

features.name: Fiat equivalents in trade review
features.description: See the approximate fiat value, in the selected base currency, of the crypto amounts quoted in a selected buy, sell or swap offer before continuing.
features.platform_notes: Desktop/web: TradingInfoItem shows a current-rate BaseCurrencyValue (with an approximation indicator) under the crypto amount of the selected offer: the receive amount for buy, the crypto amount for sell, and both send and receive amounts for swap. It is hidden while a DEX simulation is loading. Mobile: CryptoToFiatValueBadge appears beside the crypto amount on the Buy, Sell and Swap preview cards, the sell completion card and the transaction review outputs. It renders an empty box when no fiat value can be computed. On the swap preview, the receive row (badge included) is replaced by a skeleton while the DEX simulation loads, and an account card is not rendered without a Suite account. On both platforms the value is converted with the app's fiat rates in the user's base currency. It is not a provider fiat quote.

features.name: Trading temporarily unavailable notice
features.description: See a full-page notice instead of the Buy, Sell, Swap or Concierge form when that trade type, or all trading, is remotely paused or the device failed an authenticity check.
features.platform_notes: Desktop/web: TradingAvailabilityGuard wraps the Buy, Sell, Swap and Concierge pages and the account-embedded TradingFormEmbed. It replaces the form with a centered warning card (TradingUnavailableCard). There are three variants, in priority order. (1) Device compromised (@trading/device-compromised): firmware authenticity hard-failed or the discovery entropy check failed. It shows 'Your device may have been compromised' and asks the user to contact Trezor Support. (2) All trading disabled (@trading/all-disabled): the message-system flags for buy, sell and exchange are all off. It shows 'Trading is temporarily unavailable' with the shared message-system text, but only when one message disables all three types. Otherwise it shows the default 'We've paused buying, selling, and swapping for now. Your funds are safe...'. In this state the Buy/Sell/Swap/Concierge tab navigation in TradingLayout and the embed's type tabs are hidden. Concierge is exempt from this state and stays available. (3) Type disabled (@trading/type-disabled): the type's own flag is off, or a device check failed only inconclusively. It shows '<Type> is temporarily unavailable' with the message-system content or the default "We've paused <type> for now". This replaces the earlier inline warning Banner (TradingDisabled, removed in 92a2c1d819), which showed for a disabled type or any compromised device. features.name: Refresh Solana staking
features.description: Pull to refresh the Solana staking management screen to update the stake position, staking info and reward history.
features.platform_notes: Mobile only. StakingManagementScreen renders SolanaStakingRewardsList for Solana-type networks (sol, dsol) instead of the transaction list, so before 5aecb0d2e4 a Solana screen had no pull-to-refresh. A pull now runs three requests in parallel (Promise.allSettled): fetchAndUpdateAccountThunk for the account, which re-syncs its balance and stake position; refreshStakingProductInfoThunk({ force: true }) through the screen's onRefresh, which ignores the product-info maximum age; and a refetch of the Everstake rewards-history query. The rewards refetch runs only when the query is enabled, which means only for mainnet 'sol'. A devnet (dsol) pull refreshes the account and product info but leaves the rewards alone (follow-up 693ac50380). The spinner uses the brand colour and stays visible until all three settle. A failed request does not block the others. ETH and TRX management screens already had pull-to-refresh through TransactionList (onRefresh) and are not part of this intent. Desktop/web: the Solana staking dashboard has no equivalent pull-to-refresh control.

navigation.mobile: Earn tab (or Solana account) > Solana staking > staking management screen > pull down on the rewards list

evidence.detail: Tapping a staking position card on the Earn screen navigates to the StakingManagement route for the account (useStakingDetailNavigation).
Account/promo entry points open StakingManagement only when staking is active for the account; otherwise they open HowStakeWorksScreen.

Solana-type networks render SolanaStakingRewardsList with onRefresh={refreshProductInfoNow} (line 76). refreshProductInfoNow (line 46) dispatches refreshStakingProductInfoThunk({ force: true }). Other networks keep TransactionList with the same onRefresh (line 79).

handleRefresh sets isRefreshing and awaits Promise.allSettled of fetchAndUpdateAccountThunk({ accountKey }), onRefresh() and, only when rewardsQuery.isEnabled, rewardsQuery.refetch(). Then it clears isRefreshing.
FlashList refreshControl is a RefreshControl bound to isRefreshing/handleRefresh and coloured elementFillBrandBold.
refreshStakingProductInfoThunk refetches the staking product info; force sets staleTime 0 instead of PRODUCT_INFO_MAX_AGE_MS (line 153).
Rewards-history query enabled only for account.symbol === 'sol', so a devnet pull skips the rewards refetch.

Co-located Jest unit test: simulated pull on a mainnet account calls onRefresh once and issues a second rewards request. Line 90: a devnet pull calls onRefresh but makes no rewards request. Component level, not Detox E2E; not executed in this review.
Native SOL staking manual procedure covers claim/stake/unstake and the staking management screen, but has no pull-to-refresh step.

shared: mobile: The screen is wrapped in EarnPortfolioTrackerGuard; the refresh requires network access to the blockchain backend and the Everstake API, and failures are swallowed (allSettled) without an error message.

features.name: Convert a legacy DRep ID
features.description: Convert a legacy CIP-105 Cardano DRep ID typed into the custom DRep field to the CIP-129 format with one click.
features.platform_notes: Desktop and web share VotingPreferenceCard, which both the Stake ADA modal (via CardanoVotingPreference) and the Change voting preference modal mount. The Convert to new format button appears only after Choose your own DRep is selected and the entered ID decodes as a valid legacy CIP-105 ID (drep, drep_vkh or drep_script prefix, 28-byte hash) that is not already in CIP-129 form. Only the Change voting preference modal passes currentDrepId. There, a legacy ID that matches the current delegate shows the current-delegate error instead, with no button. In the Stake ADA modal no current-delegate check runs, and a legacy ID equal to the backend drep_id is converted with its has_script credential type kept. Until the user converts the ID, Stake (StakeButton isDrepValid) and Continue (StakeChangeDelegateModal invalid_drep) stay disabled. Mobile has no Cardano DRep input: ADA staking is view-only there.

navigation.desktop: Cardano account > Staking tab > Start staking > Earn in a nutshell > continue to the Stake ADA modal > Who votes with your ADA? > Choose your own DRep > enter a legacy DRep ID > Convert to new format; or, with an active delegation: Cardano account > Staking tab > Change delegate > Change voting preference > Choose your own DRep > enter a legacy DRep ID > Convert to new format
navigation.web: Cardano account > Staking tab > Start staking > Earn in a nutshell > continue to the Stake ADA modal > Who votes with your ADA? > Choose your own DRep > enter a legacy DRep ID > Convert to new format; or, with an active delegation: Cardano account > Staking tab > Change delegate > Change voting preference > Choose your own DRep > enter a legacy DRep ID > Convert to new format

evidence.detail: getConvertedDrepId normalizes the entered ID to CIP-129. If the ID matches the backend's current legacy drep_id, it uses getCardanoAccountDrepId so the has_script credential type is kept.
A valid ID that is not in CIP-129 form produces the 'DRep ID is in the legacy format' error. The current-delegate check (only when currentDrepId is passed) and the invalid-ID check run first.
handleDrepIdConvert writes the converted ID into the voting delegation state and sets the converted flag.
The legacy-format InputError has a 'Convert to new format' button (TR_STAKING_CONVERT_DREP_ID). After conversion, the field shows 'Converted to the new DRep ID format' with a check icon (line 254).

normalizeCardanoDrepId decodes CIP-129 or CIP-105 bech32 (drep, drep_vkh, drep_script) and re-encodes it as CIP-129 with a key-hash or script-hash header. isCardanoDrepIdCip129 (line 124) checks whether the ID is already canonical.
The Stake button stays disabled while a custom DRep ID is not in CIP-129 form, so the user must convert it first.
In the Change voting preference modal, Continue stays disabled with invalid_drep while the custom ID is not in CIP-129 form.
The Stake ADA form (StakeForm.tsx:54) mounts VotingPreferenceCard under the heading 'Who votes with your ADA?', without currentDrepId.
The Change voting preference modal mounts VotingPreferenceCard with currentDrepId. It opens from StakingCard 'Change delegate' (StakingCard.tsx:233) through UserContextModal.tsx:190.

Co-located component unit tests (not E2E, not executed here): a pasted legacy ID stays as entered until conversion; the convert button replaces it with the CIP-129 key ID and shows the converted message; editing clears the message; the current script delegate in legacy spelling shows no button; mixed-case input is rejected.
Cardano product descriptors set platforms.mobile.access to 'read-only'. There is no voting preference or DRep input.

features.name: TRX staking transaction history
features.description: Review a Tron account's freeze, unfreeze, vote, claim and withdraw transactions in a dedicated list on its staking detail screen.
features.platform_notes: Desktop/web: the TRX staking dashboard (Staking tab of a Tron account) refetches the full account history on mount and renders a 'Staking transactions' list below the staking cards in both the active and empty-staking states; the list is hidden when the account has no stake-type transactions, is not exportable and has no search/filter. Stake-type Tron transactions are those whose tronSpecific.contractType is FreezeBalance(V2), UnfreezeBalance(V2), VoteWitness, WithdrawExpireUnfreeze or WithdrawBalance; DelegateResource, transfers and smart-contract calls are excluded. Mobile (view-only TRX staking): StakingManagementScreen renders the native TransactionList with filter {type: 'staking'} (same shared selector) on the non-Solana branch, under the Tron resources header, with pull-to-refresh; the screen is reached only for accounts with a non-zero staked balance.

navigation.desktop: Sidebar > Tron (TRX) account > Staking tab > scroll below the staking cards to 'Staking transactions'
navigation.web: Sidebar > Tron (TRX) account > Staking tab > scroll below the staking cards to 'Staking transactions'
navigation.mobile: Home > Tron (TRX) account > staked TRX row in the account overview > staking detail > scroll to the transaction list (alternatively Earn tab > Staking positions card > TRX position)

evidence.detail: Account Staking page renders TronStakingDashboard for tron accounts that have the staking network feature.
Dashboard dispatches fetchAllTransactionsForAccountThunk (noLoading) on mount so the full history is available for the staking list.
Transactions list is rendered below the cards regardless of whether staking is active or the EmptyStakingCard is shown.

Returns null when the account has no stake-type transactions; otherwise renders TransactionList with heading TR_STAKING_TRANSACTIONS ('Staking transactions'), isExportable=false and isTxFilteringEnabled=false (lines 41-43).
selectAccountStakeTypeTransactions keeps ETH/SOL/ADA stake txs and Tron txs matched by isTronStakingTx (line 263).
TRON_STAKING_CONTRACT_TYPES: Freeze/Unfreeze (V1 and V2), VoteWitness, WithdrawExpireUnfreeze, WithdrawBalance.
Non-Solana branch renders native TransactionList with filter {type: 'staking'} (line 74) and pull-to-refresh of stake data.
Native 'staking' filter selects selectAccountStakeTypeTransactionsWithTokenTransfers, which wraps the shared selectAccountStakeTypeTransactions.
Pressing the staking row in the account overview navigates to StakingManagement for the account.
Earn staking positions bottom sheet entry navigates to the staking detail screen.
The Tron product descriptor sets platforms.mobile.access to 'read-only': the detail screen is view-only, history is visible but staking actions are not.
Unit tests: Tron freeze/unfreeze/vote/withdraw/claim txs are kept and transfer/trigger/delegate txs are omitted (line 285); selector-level only, not the user journey, not executed in this review.
Web-only Playwright test opens the TRX Staking tab with mocked freeze/vote history (so the list renders) but asserts only cards/balances; no assertion on the staking transaction list.
Manual TRX staking lifecycle opens the Staking tab but contains no step checking the staking transaction list.

ownership.basis: Inherits the team of the parent feature earn.staking.trx.

features.name: Insufficient gas balance warning
features.description: Warn during review of a dApp EVM transaction-signing request when the selected account balance cannot cover the network fee.
features.platform_notes: Shown only for ethereumSignTransaction requests that open the transaction simulation review. That happens for WalletConnect and other non-desktop-ws/non-web Connect sources on chains Blockaid can scan. Desktop/web compares the fee of the currently selected composed fee level (normal by default) with the account balance and renders a warning Banner below the Network fee card, so changing the fee level can show or hide it. Mobile has no fee picker: it multiplies the dApp-supplied gasLimit by maxFeePerGas or gasPrice and shows a BannerFull only after simulation data has loaded. Neither platform shows it for typed-data signing, when no fee or gas price is known, or for a placeholder account with an empty balance. The warning does not disable Confirm/Continue.

scale.3-4: Partial happy path; consequential outcomes or stable checks missing.
scale.5: Basic complete happy path with meaningful outcome verification.

rules: Review test bodies and called assertion/page-object helpers; mappings and title counts are only discovery aids.
Do not inherit parent references into children or use a single ancestor scenario as evidence for every descendant.
Evaluate high-level features against their meaningful intents; do not blindly average children or take their maximum.
0 is allowed and required for absent verification. Do not convert absence to 1.
Keep unavailable-platform score 0 with applicability not-supported unless a test actually verifies the unsupported-state intent.
Use active automated evidence only for positive automated scores. Preserve relevant skipped evidence with explicit caveats.
Name important uncovered intents and explain intermediate scores. Avoid unexplained high scores.
No application tests are being executed by this source-quality review.

limitations: Source-quality review only: no automated tests, app/device flows or manual procedures were executed.

Desktop scores include computer web/Electron scenarios; evidence notes web-only, desktop-only and mocked-provider limitations. Optional model-tagged tests have differing PR/nightly selection and do not imply every scenario runs on every change.
Android scores exclude iOS-only residence cases and the skipped Suite Sync describe block. Emulator-driven Android flows do not establish real USB/Bluetooth radio or OS pairing behavior.
Manual scores describe the quality of written verification steps; describe.skip is their normal procedure container, not proof of absence or execution. Placeholder files with no steps receive zero.
Unit/component tests and fixture construction are intentionally excluded from automated E2E scores.
A source search can establish no found verification, not prove no external/private manual test plan exists. No external test-management execution data was available.
Source-quality assessment only: no application, emulator, automated suite or manual procedure was executed. Scores assess checked intents, not passing rate, flakiness or runtime availability.

Desktop includes shared computer web/Electron behavior. Web-only CSV/download/BIP329/legacy-label scenarios and Electron-only pending-mining scenarios are identified in evidence. Optional model/network cases count as maintained executable coverage but are not guaranteed on every PR run.

Android selection excludes @iosOnly. Active regtest send/receive are T3T1/T3W1 and tracker tests are @noDevice; this is not proof of behavior on every Trezor model. Entire native Suite Sync describe.skip contributes no active automated credit.

Manual describe.skip containers are assessed as written procedures, not inactive automation. Broad generic instructions receive lower scores than concrete expected outcomes. Steps do not inherit assertions from automated-test references in prerequisites.

Absence means no concrete verification located during whole-suite searches plus focused body/helper review. SDK-only Connect tests, unit tests, fixtures, uninvoked helper capabilities and ancestor references do not establish UI E2E leaf coverage.

Native asset-detail generic graph wording was traced through AssetDetailHeader/AssetDetailPriceSection to AssetPriceChart; it covers only range selection/persistence, not historical market data. Initial camera permission grant is not restored-permission coverage.

Android Send happy-path quality credits the helper wait for TransactionDetail as a successful broadcast outcome: source tracing shows navigation requires the fulfilled send txid. This does not establish correctness of detail amounts/fees/status fields or the contents of review screens.
Static source-quality review only; no tests executed. Scores do not measure pass rate, stability or execution recency.
Desktop combines computer web/Electron. Yield/TRX and some trading/history scenarios are webOnly; SDK permission scenarios desktopOnly. Scores do not imply every project runs all checks.
Android excludes iosOnly residence tests through runner grep. No active automated native staking/yield tests found.
Trade/staking/yield use controlled provider/chain/broadcast state. Verified UI/device and mock-driven results do not establish real provider payment/settlement.
Manual describe.skip is the procedure container convention. Scores measure written quality without claiming execution. Conditional optional steps limit completeness.
